findings.finding: The Published cells say not established where the source actually reports a qualitative or multicomponent claim. Absence of a justified scalar aggregate is not absence of the original reported finding. Column heading and cell wording conflate applicability with evidence status; source claims/values must be explicit. Ours cells also need to communicate conditional support versus incomplete replication independently of absent aggregate magnitude.

affected_rows.source_statement: Under a common appropriately identified IRT measurement scale, biometric conclusions are asserted to be independent of the particular item subset.
Incorporating an IRT measurement model remedies the scale-induced interaction bias and recovers generating parameters in the studied designs.
The proposed method has useful power to detect genotype–environment interaction under the investigated sample-size and effect-size conditions.
Sum-score analysis can produce spurious genotype–environment interaction from measurement-scale properties.
The28-item scale measures two distinct dimensions: liberalism–conservatism and use of the question-mark response.
Nine selected items constitute the proposed ordinal social-liberalism subscale.
The interaction point-estimate direction changes between IRT and sum-score analyses: beta1
The interaction point-estimate direction changes between IRT and sum-score analyses: gamma1
The alternative logvariance ACE×M model is asserted to be uniquely identified.
Simultaneous IRT and ACE×M modelling is asserted to prevent spurious moderation arising from heterogeneous measurement error.
The source states the logvariance model has only one maximum in its likelihood function.
Large samples are said to be necessary to detect beta1a moderation.
Large samples are said to be necessary to detect beta1c moderation.
As few as20phenotypic items are asserted sufficient to find moderation effects.
None of the thirteen measured covariate coefficients was detected in the educational-achievement application using the reported99.6%HPD criterion.
The source asserts that full information is more powerful than deletion regardless of the investigated missingness mechanism, covariate count or amount of missingness.
Full information gives lower variance-component standard errors than deletion across the investigated missingness mechanisms and design grid.
The full-information model uses all observed phenotype and covariate components when covariate data are incomplete.
MAR deletion underestimates A variance while full information remains close to the generating value.
MAR deletion underestimates C variance while full information remains close to the generating value.
MAR deletion overestimates heritability while full information remains close to the generating value.
